MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  APRIL 6, 2022

CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting of the
City of Rolling Hills Estates at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Stegura, Bacinski, Bain, Chuang, Friedman*,
  Olson*, O’Malley*, Radocchio, Tarr

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Larson, Low, Uppal

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

* Joined the meeting after Approval of Minutes.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, MARCH 9,
  2022

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHUANG made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN
to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 9, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES TURF REMOVAL PROGRAM

Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. CalWater is
working with staff to identify opportunities for addressing irrigation inefficiencies and the removal
of turf to be replaced with drought tolerant plants at City Hall and Highridge Park. The City Council
is going to be reviewing the proposal in April. Staff would like to know if there is any interest from
EAC Members to serve on a Landscape Design Subcommittee for this project (the City Council
has not confirmed if a subcommittee will be created for this project).

CHAIR STEGURA added that this item has already been presented to the Parks and Activities
Commission. Committee Member Bain will be a member of the subcommittee; this will be a joint
subcommittee between the EAC and the Parks and Activities Commission.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired if the City may solicit community members who may have
expertise in this area. CHAIR STEGURA responded that there is interest in working with the PVP
Land Conservancy; in addition, the city has a professional landscaping service that staff may
reach out to.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN, Planning Manager Naughton stated
that the installation date is by the end of August. Also, this is a rebate program which will require
formal approval by CalWater on the plantings and cost before the City would expend the money
for this program.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN stated that the rebate proposed for City Hall is over $93K and the
rebate for Highridge Park is over $144K; with this considerable amount, this will allow for
spectacular work and make City Hall a showcase for this type of installation.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  1
 MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 9, 2022
 CHAIR STEGURA asked the committee members who may know of community members who
have expertise in this type of work to email her and Planning Manager Naughton.

The Committee Members who volunteered to be on the subcommittee are as follows:

  •  CHAIR STEGURA
  •  COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN
  •  COMMITTEE MEMBER O’MALLEY
  •  COMMITTEE MEMBER CHUANG

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN stated that she will follow-up with Assistant City Manager Davis
regarding the status of the project.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA requested that all email correspondence regarding this
matter be sent to Assistant City Manager Davis and that she be copied.

B.  WATER SHORTAGE RESPONSE LEVEL 2

Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation with a summary of the staff report. On
March 15, 2022 CalWater filed Advice Letter No. 2446 requesting activation of Stage 2 of the
“Water Use Restrictions of its Water Shortage Contingency Plan”. On March 28, 2022, the
governor signed Executive Order N-7-22, which in part calls on the State’s Water Resources
Control Board to consider requiring that urban water suppliers operate at a Level 2 of their
“Customized Water Shortage Contingency Plan”. If approved by the CPUC, the measures would
go into effect on April 15, 2022.

Planning Manager Naughton stated provided an overview of how this will affect residential
customers. She also shared CalWater’s Conservation web page, which provides various helpful
tips and programs offered.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, stated that CalWater will be
working on brochures that can go up on the City’s website and be sent via social media.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHUANG asked for clarification on watering restrictions for Level 2.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that this specific filing is for two times per week.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
RADOCCHIO to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION THAT THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE DIRECT STAFF TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION FOR ADOPTION BY THE
  CITY COUNCIL, DECLARING A WATER SHORTAGE RESPONSE LEVEL 2,
  CONSISTENT WITH CAL WATER’S ADVISE LETTER NO. 2446.

The Committee approved the motion with a vote of 8; 1 committee member abstained.

6.  MANAGER ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA reported on City Council’s action on the EAC’s
recommendation that the California Power Alliance (CPA) default rate for non-residential
customers remain at 50%. The City Council discussed this and a motion was made for non-
residential customers to remain at 50%, and the motion failed. Another motion was made for non-
residential customers to move the default rate to 100%, and that motion passed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO asked if the City will be informing the businesses that the
default rate will be moved to 100%. CHAIR STEGURA stated that businesses will be notified by
the CPA. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the PVP Chamber of Commerce is aware of
this decision and the City is in communication with them to disseminate this information to the
larger customers, including the school district. The City will work with customers to help them with
the level that works best for them.

COMMITTEE MEMBER TARR stated that he would like to discuss PFAS Air Emissions at the
Palos Verdes Landfill and their potential to cause negative health impacts on people who live
around the landfill. CHAIR STEGURA stated that Committee Member Tarr is working with staff

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  2
 MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 9, 2022
 on answers to this question. The EAC is an advisory committee to the City Council, and they can
take action on items that are under the City’s jurisdiction. The Landfill and PFAS issues are within
the jurisdiction of the Sanitation District.

COMMITTEE MEMBER TARR made a recommendation that the item regarding PFAS be
agendized.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BAIN to,

  ADJOURN THE EAC MEETING AT 8:15 p.m.

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

_____________________________  ____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Debby Stegura, Chair

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
